paper.title: Lyudmilovsk Pravda, today's issue
paper.inside: Inside: the town chronicle, tomorrow's weather and tides, holidays, the cinema and the small ads.
paper.front.fest_today.1: Today: {0}! The editors wish the town a happy day and remind you that a holiday looks best from the square, not the window.
paper.front.fest_today.2: {0}: the town is dressed up from the morning. The street sweepers were out early, the bakers earlier, and the children seem not to have gone to bed at all.
paper.front.fest_today.3: A holiday at the door: {0}. Our correspondent walked the promenade and reports that everyone is smiling except the gulls, and the gulls are always like that.
paper.front.fest_more.1: {0} goes on. If you missed it yesterday, today is not too late.
paper.front.fest_more.2: {0}, day two, and the town is not tired yet. The refreshment stalls ask you to bring your own mugs: there aren't enough glasses to go round.
paper.front.fest_tomorrow.1: Tomorrow: {0}. The town is getting ready: hammers on the square, dough in the bakeries.
paper.front.fest_tomorrow.2: Tomorrow: {0}. The editors advise a good night's sleep tonight; tomorrow there'll be no time.
paper.front.fest_soon.1: Coming soon: {0}. The clubs are sewing, gluing and rehearsing; people are already asking the shops for candles and flags.
paper.front.fest_soon.2: In a few days: {0}. The committee is looking for volunteers to carry, hang and smile.
paper.front.tamed_swan.1: Schoolboy tames a swan! Yesterday on the shore a mute swan took food straight from the palm of one of our young townsfolk. The ornithologists throw up their hands; the swan, its wings.
paper.front.tamed_swan.2: A swan that eats from the hand. Yesterday's witnesses say the mute swan did not hiss once. The editors are waiting for a photograph and promise it the front page.
paper.front.record.1: A record catch! {0}, {1} g: nothing like it has been landed from the pier before. The angler, a schoolboy, declined an interview: he was hurrying home before the fish nodded off.
paper.front.record.2: A new record: {0}, {1} g. The old anglers on the pier say the fish were bigger in their day. They admit they weighed them by eye.
paper.front.tamed.1: The young naturalist's new friend: {0}. Yesterday the bird ate from his hand for the first time. The editors ask the neighbours not to scare the friendship away.
paper.front.tamed.2: From the hand, without fear: {0}. A schoolboy with a pocket full of seeds did yesterday what grown-ups lack the patience for.
paper.front.rare.1: A rare visitor on the coast: {0}. A young watcher with binoculars spotted the bird yesterday. The ornithologists of Academgorodok ask to be told of any further sightings.
paper.front.rare.2: Look who flew in: {0}! Such a bird is seldom seen in Lyudmilovsk. One young reader not only saw it but wrote it down in his notebook.
paper.front.quest.1: Seen through to the end: “{0}”. The editors have it from reliable sources and say thank you on behalf of the town.
paper.front.quest.2: Good news: “{0}” is done. They say a schoolboy who is always in a hurry somewhere lent a hand.
paper.front.catch.1: A good day on the pier: {0}, {1} g. The catch was shown to the whole jetty and then, they say, to grandmother as well.
paper.front.catch.2: A bite! {0}, {1} g. Yesterday's catch by a schoolboy is the talk of the bread queue.
paper.front.weather_first_snow.1: First snow! The forecasters promise it will settle tomorrow. The sweepers are taking out shovels, the children sledges, and the cats sit at the window in disbelief.
paper.front.weather_first_snow.2: Winter is here: tomorrow the town will wake up white. The cable car is running but asks passengers to hold on to the handrails.
paper.front.weather_thunder.1: Thunderstorms tomorrow. The forecasters advise not sheltering under a lone tree on the shore and not swimming while it rumbles.
paper.front.weather_thunder.2: A storm is gathering over the sea: tomorrow {0} to {1} °C, loud and wet. The cinema has added a matinee for the occasion.
paper.front.weather_storm.1: Gale warning! Tomorrow the wind will reach {2} m/s. Boats are being hauled up, washing taken in from balconies, hats held on by hand.
paper.front.weather_storm.2: A gale is coming ashore: up to {2} m/s tomorrow. The lifeguard station asks you to keep away from the end of the breakwater: today the waves are in charge.
paper.front.weather_heat.1: Heat! Up to {1} °C tomorrow. The kvass on the promenade has been ordered a week ahead, and the ice-cream lady asks people not to crowd.
paper.front.weather_heat.2: The town is melting: {1} °C in the shade tomorrow. The clinic reminds you of sun hats, and the sea reminds you of itself.
paper.front.weather_frost.1: Frost! Down to {0} °C tomorrow. The bay may freeze near the shore, but the editors advise staying off the ice until the lifeguard station says so.
paper.front.weather_frost.2: A crackling frost: {0} °C tomorrow. The sparrows sit like little balls, the cable car heats its cabins, and the Saucer café fills the tea to the brim.
paper.front.weather_fog.1: Fog tomorrow. The lighthouse will sound its horn, the boats will wait, and the promenade will look like another town.
paper.front.weather_fog.2: Sea fog: tomorrow you'll see as far as the next lamp post. Cyclists are asked to ring their bells, and walkers not to jump when they do.
paper.brief.tamed: Bird news: {0} now takes food from one schoolboy's hand. Both sides are pleased.
paper.brief.rare: A rare bird: a young watcher recorded one on the coast: {0}.
paper.brief.seen: A new entry in the young naturalist's notebook: {0}.
paper.brief.quest: A good deed: “{0}” has been seen through. The editors are grateful.
paper.brief.catch: From the pier: {0}, {1} g. The angler asked us not to print his name.
paper.front.cup.1: The cup goes to a newcomer! {0} was won by a schoolboy. His opponent in the final, {1}, shook his hand and asked for the game to be written down for study.
paper.front.cup.2: A sensation at the club: {0} went to a young entrant. The regulars can't remember the last time the cup went so early. The finalist: {1}.
paper.front.cup.3: A new name on the cup. {0}: the winner is a schoolboy; the experienced finalist ({1}) gave way. The cup stands on the shelf beside the old ones.
paper.cup.hero_won: {0}: won by a young entrant, a schoolboy. Congratulations from the editors.
paper.cup.hero_out.0: The tournament's young entrant went out in the first round but promised to be back next week.
paper.cup.hero_out.1: The young entrant reached the semi-finals. The editors are following his progress.
paper.cup.hero_out.2: The young entrant reached the final and lost only the last game.
paper.cup.today: Today: {0}, starting at {1}. Venue: {2}. Sign up at the bracket board before the start.
paper.brief.win: News from the club: a schoolboy beat one of the regulars. The regular demands a rematch.
paper.bday.plain: Happy birthday to {0}, who is {1} today.
paper.bday.jubilee: A round birthday: {0} turns {1}! The neighbours in the block are collecting for a cake.
paper.bday.child: {0} is {1} today! Wishing you sunshine, ice cream and a fair wind.
paper.wed.plain: {0} and {1} celebrate {2} years of marriage today. Love and happiness!
paper.wed.silver: A silver wedding: {0} and {1} have been together for {2} years. Congratulations!
paper.wed.golden: A golden wedding! {0} and {1} have been together for {2} years. The whole building is invited for pies.
paper.weather.drizzle: Tomorrow: drizzle, {0} to {1} °C. An umbrella is optional but pleasant.
paper.weather.rain: Tomorrow: rain, {0} to {1} °C. Take an umbrella.
paper.weather.unknown: The forecasters are silent: the barometer in our office is stuck again.
paper.wind.calm: Calm: the flags hang still and the gulls go on foot.
paper.sea.swim: Sea temperature: {0} °C, good for a swim.
paper.aurora: Northern lights are possible tonight: the astronomy club advises looking north after midnight.
paper.bite: For anglers: better bites than usual from {0}.
paper.bite.none: For anglers: steady bites, no surprises.
paper.soon.none: No holidays in the next two weeks. But there's the fair at weekends.
paper.newsreel: Before every showing, old films: {0}, with the projectionist's comments.
paper.archive.head: The Lyudmilovsk Pravda on file. Issues kept: {0}. Read by you: {1}.
paper.read: Read an issue of the Lyudmilovsk Pravda: {0} of {1} on file
dev.action.paper.print: Paper: 7 days of issues to the log
paper.fest.bird_day.1: Bird Day! Schoolchildren are putting up nest boxes, the library has an exhibition, “Who lives outside our window”, and the feeders are especially busy with people and birds.
paper.fest.bird_day.2: Bird Day today. The ornithologists of Academgorodok remind you: bread is bad for birds, seeds should be unsalted, and patience is free.
paper.fest.christmas.1: Christmas in Lyudmilovsk: candles in the windows, gingerbread in the bakeries, and the choir rehearsed so long it now sings in its sleep.
paper.fest.christmas.2: A quiet holiday: Christmas. The editors wish everyone a warm home, hot tea and neighbours who say hello first.
paper.fest.fisherman_day.1: Fisherman's Day! Contests on the pier: the biggest fish, the smallest fish, and the longest story about the one that got away.
paper.fest.fisherman_day.2: Fisherman's Day today. The fish stalls at the market are selling at a discount, and the town's oldest angler will show how to tie a knot that never comes undone.
paper.fest.lantern_night.1: Lantern Night: tonight hundreds of lights will rise from the beach. Make your wishes in advance: a lantern flies fast.
paper.fest.lantern_night.2: Lantern Night tonight. The wind, they forecast, blows off the shore, so the lanterns will go out over the bay. The fire brigade asks you to launch them only from the beach.
paper.fest.maslenitsa.1: Maslenitsa! Every café is making pancakes, the effigy is being readied on the square, and the ice slide by the school is open till dark.
paper.fest.maslenitsa.2: Maslenitsa in full swing in Lyudmilovsk: a pancake with caviar, a pancake with jam and a pancake just because. The editors recommend the third.
paper.fest.midsummer.1: Midsummer Night: the sun will hardly set. The townsfolk gather on the shore to meet the dawn, which will come very early.
paper.fest.midsummer.2: The shortest night of the year. Bonfires on the beach, wreaths on the water, and a sun that leaves only briefly, like a guest stepping into the hall.
paper.fest.new_year.1: Happy New Year, Lyudmilovsk! The tree on the square lit up at midnight sharp, the fireworks could be seen even from the cable car, and the last tram, which we haven't got, was late anyway.
paper.fest.new_year.2: New Year in town: every staircase smells of tangerines, and the editors wish everyone a year as warm as the sun over the bay.
paper.fest.perseids.1: Perseid Night: stars will be falling till morning. The astronomy club is taking its telescopes to the shore; the promenade lamps are promised to go dark.
paper.fest.perseids.2: A meteor shower! Best watched after midnight, lying on the warm sand. Make your wishes quickly: a meteor won't wait.
paper.fest.sea_festival.1: The Sea Festival! A parade of boats on the promenade, an angling contest on the pier, and lights over the water tonight. The lifeguards are on duty all day.
paper.fest.sea_festival.2: Today the sea is the town's guest: the Sea Festival has brought everyone to the shore. The editors ask you not to throw plastic bags in along with the wreaths.
paper.story.1: The cable car breaks a record: last week its cabins carried as many passengers as the town has residents. Some of them, admittedly, several times over.
paper.story.2: Kesha the parrot calls the stops again. At the Saucer café you hear “Next stop, the Saucer!” The management asks visitors to stay seated: nobody has to go anywhere.
paper.story.3: The sun is closer than it looks. The Academgorodok observatory told our readers why sunset over the bay lasts longer than over any other town. The explanation took three pages; the answer, one smile.
paper.story.4: The library stays open longer: the reading room is now open until nine in the evening. The librarian asks you not to rustle pages too loudly, even the exciting ones.
paper.story.5: The pier is repaired. New boards, freshly painted rails, and the bench where the same angler always sits was left as it was, at his request.
paper.story.6: Chess tournament at the Cog club. Retired Aristarkh Lvovich won; second place went to his grandson, third to the cat that sat on the board throughout.
paper.story.7: The Druzhba sanatorium invites you. The spring is warm, the treatments pleasant, and the talk in the queue free and good for you.
paper.story.8: A new walk. The local historians suggest going from the club along the cliff to town: two hours, three benches and one view that won't fit in a camera.
paper.story.9: The youth orchestra seeks a trombonist. There are drummers, there are violinists, and enthusiasm to spare. One person with strong lungs is needed.
paper.story.10: The starlings are back! The first flocks are already circling over the beach. The ornithologists ask you to check the nest boxes: the tenants are on their way.
paper.story.11: The lilac is out. The yards on the Terraces smell so good that passers-by slow down. The editors received three letters asking people not to break off branches, and one asking to be allowed.
paper.story.12: The swimming season is open. The lifeguard station has raised its flag, the ice-cream lady her menu, and the sea its best weather.
paper.story.13: Poplar fluff on the promenade. The sweepers sweep, the wind blows it back. The score so far is in the wind's favour.
paper.story.14: White nights. The promenade lamps go on an hour later, and the children assure their parents it's still light and far too early for bed.
paper.story.15: Jellyfish near the shore: harmless, round and see-through. The scientists ask you not to pull them up on the sand: they get bored there.
paper.story.16: Amber after the storm. Amber is turning up on the beach again. The biggest piece, the size of a thimble, was brought to our office; we gave it back so the finder can keep looking.
paper.story.17: Mushroom season. The wood beyond Academgorodok is full of mushroom pickers. The clinic reminds you that unfamiliar mushrooms are for pictures only.
paper.story.18: The first of September. The school opened its doors, the first-graders brought flowers, and the teachers brought patience for a whole year.
paper.story.19: Leaf fall in the park. The sweepers have declared a truce with the maples until the end of October. The children jump into the piles, and the sweepers pretend not to see.
paper.story.20: Cranes over the bay. A skein flew over town yesterday. Our photographer caught half of it; the other half flew off.
paper.story.21: The waxwings have come. The rowans in the yards are covered with pink crested guests. Listen: they ring like little bells.
paper.story.22: The rink is ready. The park pond has frozen properly; hockey players mark out goals, skaters draw circles, and the veterans draw memories.
paper.story.23: The Christmas tree market is open. Firs from the northern forestry, honestly fluffy. The seller promises every one will last till the Old New Year.
paper.story.24: A record snowman. In a yard on Novikova Street the children built a snowman as tall as a lamp post. The vegetable stall donated the carrot.
paper.story.25: The thaw. Icicles are melting, the roofs are dripping, and the cats cross the street in the middle, well away from the eaves.
paper.story.26: The ice is moving on the Ural. The river in the east has shed its ice. Whole families come to watch; it moves slowly and grandly, as if on parade.
paper.story.27: Clean-up day. The residents of the Terraces came out to plant trees along the stairways. Twenty limes planted, forty cups of tea drunk.
paper.town.1: The department store's lost property: a yellow umbrella has stood there a month. The owner is known but asks for it not to be returned: passers-by smile at it.
paper.town.2: The jam contest is postponed: the jury can't decide whether pine-cone jam counts as jam.
paper.town.3: The Rassvet's projectionist asks for the reel with the film's third part back: “We know the beginning and the end; the middle we remember dimly.”
paper.town.4: A talking scale has appeared at the market: it says the weight out loud. The sellers are unhappy: it's more honest than they'd like.
paper.town.5: The post office reminds you: postcards of Lyudmilovsk are on sale again. The gull stamps are sold out; the lighthouse ones remain.
paper.town.6: The culture house choir rehearses on Thursdays. Come and sing; if you're shy, come and listen: that helps too.
paper.town.7: The Cog club has started a repair circle: bring something broken, take home something working and one new skill.
paper.town.8: The barber on the promenade has introduced the “sunset cut”: the same haircut, but at a discount and with a view.
paper.town.9: The bakery on the Terraces has a new loaf, the “Pebble”. The crust crunches like pebbles underfoot.
paper.town.10: The boat station: rowing boats for hire at the old price. A life jacket is free and compulsory.
paper.town.11: The observatory holds an open evening: the Moon, Saturn and tea. Tea as you wish; Saturn as the weather allows.
paper.town.12: The school wall paper ran a column, “Why is the sky blue?” Twelve answers came in: three correct, all of them lovely.
paper.town.13: The lifeguard station held a drill. The dummy was rescued in forty seconds; the dummy has no complaints.
paper.town.14: The playground by the school has new swings. The queue for them is longer than for the buffet.
paper.town.15: A mitten was found on the cable car. It seeks its owner. Description: left-handed, knitted, very lonely.
paper.town.16: The sanatorium got a new batch of deckchairs. The old ones are moving to the beach, where, they say, they belong.
paper.town.17: The Harvest Fair is getting ready: the Terraces' gardeners promise a pumpkin the size of a boat. The boat station is on its guard.
paper.town.18: The street sweepers ask townsfolk not to feed the gulls chips: afterwards the gulls won't eat fish.
paper.town.19: A new exhibition at the library: “Books read in queues”. The exhibits are crumpled but content.
paper.town.20: The Academgorodok weather station has put up a new weathervane. The old one, they say, always pointed at the café.
paper.town.21: The ice slide in the school yard is open. Sledging mats are lent from the cloakroom on your word of honour.
paper.town.22: The Rassvet's photo circle announces a contest, “The town in a window”. Photos accepted till the end of the month.
paper.town.23: The music school: scales drift from its windows in the evenings. The neighbours can already tell the pupils apart by their mistakes.
paper.town.24: A bottle with a letter was found on the beach. The letter is in Swedish and, by all appearances, about the weather.
paper.town.25: Before its showings the Rassvet now runs an old newsreel. At “The Arrival of a Train” the hall still ducks, though the train is over a hundred years old.
paper.town.26: The Rassvet's projectionist reads his own comments over the old films. The audience begs him to go on: “Without him the Moon would be just the Moon.”
paper.town.27: Ticket machines now stand on the platforms. Five roubles and the ride is lawful. Conductor Auntie Valya warns you once; Timofeich, never.
paper.town.28: The train's ticket punch has been replaced. The new one clicks so loudly that passengers at the window wake up, and fare dodgers all the more.
paper.town.29: The Cog club chess tournament went ahead in the usual Saturday way. A pensioner from the Terraces won; second place went to his grandson, who had been prompting him.
paper.town.30: A dominoes tournament was played in the sanatorium's pump room. The clatter of tiles drowned out the mineral spring; the spring took offence and now gurgles louder.
paper.town.31: Windy: kites are over the cliff again. The children fly them; the grown-ups hold the reels and pretend it is for the children.
paper.town.32: The postman's son's kite is stuck in the poplar by the post office. No one will take it down: “Let it hang; the wind will give it back.”
paper.town.33: Radio Lyudmilovsk Wave asks listeners for requests. The most requested item is the silence before the weather forecast.
paper.town.34: The department store sells records again. The shop assistant puts each one on the player first: “A record must be heard out before it is handed over.”
paper.town.35: The post office notes a rise in letters. People write postcards even to neighbours across the street: “It's more interesting than knocking.”
paper.town.36: New benches stand in the park by the library. The librarian lets you read the reading-room books on them: “Just not in the wind.”
paper.town.37: The sanatorium has issued its first cure diploma: nine stamps, not one treatment missed. The graduate promises to return, for a second course.
paper.town.38: The piano at the culture house has been tuned. Now anyone passing plays it; the porter can now recognise “Chopsticks” in six different renditions.
paper.town.39: Getting ready for Big Sun Day: bunting is going up in the streets. Old-timers advise a stock of dark glasses and good spirits.
paper.town.40: The paper's poll: where is the best tea in town? Not the buffet, not the Yantar, but “at the neighbour's, if she asks you in.”
paper.ad.1: Will swap an aquarium for a bicycle. No fish, please.
paper.ad.2: Seeking a dominoes partner. A patient one.
paper.ad.3: Kittens free to a good home. The kittens are ginger; warm hands preferred.
paper.ad.4: Will buy old postcards of the coast.
paper.ad.5: Dog lost; answers to “Sharik” and to a rustling bag.
paper.ad.6: Guitar lessons. Three chords in an evening, the rest by summer.
paper.ad.7: Watch repairs. Fast. Well, not very fast, but precise.
paper.ad.8: Corner of a studio to let to a painter. Quiet and sea view included.
paper.ad.9: Whoever found a blue bobble hat, please return it: it's a favourite.
paper.ad.10: The Surf choir invites basses. Tenors too, but there are plenty already.
paper.ad.11: Boat for sale. It floats. Tested.
paper.ad.12: Will swap a two-room flat on the Terraces for one room with a lighthouse view.
paper.ad.13: Seeking a companion for the cable car to Academgorodok. Afraid of heights, but curious.
paper.ad.14: Socks knitted to order. Any size except someone else's.
paper.ad.15: Whoever saw a speckled hen by the market: she isn't lost, she's out for a walk. Please don't catch her.
paper.ad.17: Sledge for sale, nearly new. Used twice, happily both times.
paper.ad.18: Pensioner seeks company for walks by the sea. I talk a lot, and listen too.
paper.ad.19: Piano free to whoever collects it from the fifth floor.
paper.ad.20: Will buy a fishing rod for my grandson. Preferably with a story.
paper.ad.21: The young naturalists' circle is recruiting. Binoculars welcome, curiosity compulsory.
paper.ad.22: Ginger cat found. Owner, the cat is waiting for you by the bakery and seems in no hurry.
paper.ad.23: Will swap lighthouse stamps for bird stamps. Gulls don't count.
paper.ad.24: Deckchair to let for the season. With a view.
paper.ad.25: Looking for whoever sang on the promenade yesterday. You were off-key, but it was lovely.
